title: The Strand Is Chosen at the Start

scenes.tts: Both DNA strands carry complementary information. How does a cell choose which strand the polymerase reads? Watch the same polymerase approach a stretch of duplex with no promoter marked. It could face either way, so these base pairs alone give us no answer.
scenes.caption: Both DNA strands carry complementary information. How does a cell choose which strand the polymerase reads? Watch the same polymerase approach a stretch of duplex with no promoter marked. It could face either way, so these base pairs alone give us no answer.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP for both films: template DNA blue, coding DNA gold, RNA green, promoter teal, polymerase white. Fill most of the frame with one schematic DNA duplex with no promoter drawn. A white polymerase block drifts toward it, flips orientation twice, and leaves moving question arrows above both strands. Label the whole drawing 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Both DNA strands carry complementary information. How does a cell choose which strand the polymerase reads? Watch the same polymerase approach a stretch of duplex with no promoter marked. It could face either way, so these base pairs alone give us no answer.

scenes.visual: The duplex compresses into a thin line below the centered title 'The Strand Is Chosen at the Start'. Keep the title alone for two seconds, then transform the line back into the same full-frame duplex.

scenes.tts: A promoter changes that. It is a DNA site where initiation machinery assembles. Its orientation places polymerase at a start site, facing downstream. The polymerase opens a short bubble. One strand enters the active site as the template.
scenes.caption: A promoter changes that. It is a DNA site where initiation machinery assembles. Its orientation places polymerase at a start site, facing downstream. The polymerase opens a short bubble. One strand enters the active site as the template.
scenes.visual: A large teal directional promoter block grows from the duplex. The white polymerase rotates to match its arrow, locks over a marked start, and opens a moving bubble. The lower strand bends into the active-site slot and turns blue; the upper strand turns gold.
scenes.narration: A promoter changes that. It is a DNA site where initiation machinery assembles. Its orientation places polymerase at a start site, facing downstream. The polymerase opens a short bubble. One strand enters the active site as the template.

scenes.tts: RNA polymerase matches RNA letters to the template, joining each new letter to the growing three prime end. The RNA pairs antiparallel with the template, running in the opposite direction like the two DNA strands. So as RNA grows five prime to three prime, polymerase reads the template three prime to five prime.
scenes.caption: RNA polymerase matches RNA letters to the template, joining each new letter to the growing three prime end. The RNA pairs antiparallel with the template, running in the opposite direction like the two DNA strands. So as RNA grows five prime to three prime, polymerase reads the template three prime to five prime.
scenes.visual: Green RNA tiles pair transiently with blue template tiles inside the moving white block. New green tiles attach only at the glowing 3′ end. Direction arrows travel with the polymerase while the fixed 5′ RNA end trails behind. Show the blue template and green RNA side by side with opposite direction arrows and a 5′ label facing a 3′ label at each end as antiparallel pairing is spoken.
scenes.narration: RNA polymerase matches RNA letters to the template, joining each new letter to the growing three prime end. The RNA pairs antiparallel with the template, running in the opposite direction like the two DNA strands. So as RNA grows five prime to three prime, polymerase reads the template three prime to five prime.

scenes.tts: Suppose the promoter points the other way on the same duplex. Which strand will enter the active site, and which way will RNA grow?
scenes.caption: Suppose the promoter points the other way on the same duplex. Which strand will enter the active site, and which way will RNA grow?
scenes.visual: Freeze the duplex, replace the promoter with a teal arrow pointing the opposite way, and show two large possible polymerase orientations. Put the question between them while a small thinking pulse moves around the promoter.
scenes.narration: Suppose the promoter points the other way on the same duplex. Which strand will enter the active site, and which way will RNA grow?

scenes.visual: Keep the predict question and both choices visible. Slowly brighten the reversed teal promoter while the two polymerase choices gently bob; reveal no answer during the pause.

scenes.tts: The whole arrangement reverses. The other DNA strand becomes the template, and the polymerase travels in the opposite direction. Chemistry has not changed. RNA still grows five prime to three prime. Flipping the start's orientation changed both the strand read and the direction of travel.
scenes.caption: The whole arrangement reverses. The other DNA strand becomes the template, and the polymerase travels in the opposite direction. Chemistry has not changed. RNA still grows 5′ to 3′. Flipping the start's orientation changed both the strand read and the direction of travel.
scenes.visual: Select the polymerase aligned with the reversed promoter. Keep the duplex fixed in place; flip only the teal promoter and the white polymerase. The strand that was gold turns blue (the new template), the strand that was blue turns gold, and the polymerase runs the opposite way. A green RNA grows from its 3′ end without changing the direction label.
scenes.narration: The whole arrangement reverses. The other DNA strand becomes the template, and the polymerase travels in the opposite direction. Chemistry has not changed. RNA still grows 5′ to 3′. Flipping the start's orientation changed both the strand read and the direction of travel.

scenes.tts: The DNA strand not used as the template is the coding strand. Read in the same direction as RNA, its sequence matches the RNA. RNA uses U where DNA uses T. The RNA pairs with the template instead, so those strands are complementary and antiparallel.
scenes.caption: The DNA strand not used as the template is the coding strand. Read in the same direction as RNA, its sequence matches the RNA. RNA uses U where DNA uses T. The RNA pairs with the template instead, so those strands are complementary and antiparallel.
scenes.visual: Carry the same bubble into a close view. Gold coding tiles and green RNA tiles slide into parallel rows and matching positions glow, with U and T swapping. Then green RNA moves beneath blue template tiles; paired positions connect while opposite direction arrows appear.
scenes.narration: The DNA strand not used as the template is the coding strand. Read in the same direction as RNA, its sequence matches the RNA. RNA uses U where DNA uses T. The RNA pairs with the template instead, so those strands are complementary and antiparallel.

scenes.tts: Now remove the promoter and RNA, leaving only the duplex. The template label becomes uncertain again. An RNA product can restore the answer because it matches coding DNA and pairs with template DNA.
scenes.caption: Now remove the promoter and RNA, leaving only the duplex. The template label becomes uncertain again. An RNA product can restore the answer because it matches coding DNA and pairs with template DNA.
scenes.visual: Fade out the teal promoter and green RNA. Blue and gold drain to white as the template tag jumps between strands. Bring back only a green RNA strip; it aligns with one strand by matching and with the other by pairing, restoring gold and blue.
scenes.narration: Now remove the promoter and RNA, leaving only the duplex. The template label becomes uncertain again. An RNA product can restore the answer because it matches coding DNA and pairs with template DNA.

scenes.tts: DNA opens ahead of polymerase and closes behind it. The growing RNA peels away through a separate path. Polymerase reads one strand while preserving the other strand's sequence in RNA.
scenes.caption: DNA opens ahead of polymerase and closes behind it. The growing RNA peels away through a separate path. Polymerase reads one strand while preserving the other strand's sequence in RNA.
scenes.visual: Zoom out so the moving bubble fills the width. Ahead, paired DNA tiles unzip into the white polymerase; behind, blue and gold tiles rejoin. Green RNA curves out through its own exit. Keep a visible 'schematic' label beside the block.
scenes.narration: DNA opens ahead of polymerase and closes behind it. The growing RNA peels away through a separate path. Polymerase reads one strand while preserving the other strand's sequence in RNA.

scenes.tts: Use these checks on any sequence. Write both DNA strands five prime to three prime. Match RNA to coding DNA after swapping U for T. Then confirm that RNA pairs antiparallel to the template. Together, these checks give the direction of travel. The polymerase moves toward the template's five prime end.
scenes.caption: Use these checks on any sequence. Write both DNA strands 5′ to 3′. Match RNA to coding DNA after swapping U for T. Then confirm that RNA pairs antiparallel to the template. Together, these checks give the direction of travel. The polymerase moves toward the template's 5′ end.
scenes.visual: Transform the moving world into three large connected checkpoints, never more than three on screen: orient both strands, match coding to RNA, pair template to RNA. A green pulse travels through them and ends as a direction arrow.
scenes.narration: Use these checks on any sequence. Write both DNA strands 5′ to 3′. Match RNA to coding DNA after swapping U for T. Then confirm that RNA pairs antiparallel to the template. Together, these checks give the direction of travel. The polymerase moves toward the template's 5′ end.

scenes.tts: This rule applies whenever RNA is copied from double stranded DNA. Promoters vary, and different cells use different initiation proteins. Yet once a start and its direction are set, RNA grows by adding to its three prime end. Antiparallel pairing then makes the polymerase read the template three prime to five prime.
scenes.caption: This rule applies whenever RNA is copied from double-stranded DNA. Promoters vary, and different cells use different initiation proteins. Yet once a start and its direction are set, RNA grows by adding to its 3′ end. Antiparallel pairing then makes the polymerase read the template 3′ to 5′.
scenes.visual: The single promoter smoothly transforms through several differently shaped teal promoter blocks while the same blue-template, gold-coding and green-RNA motion continues. End with the start marker glowing and both direction arrows locked in place.
scenes.narration: This rule applies whenever RNA is copied from double-stranded DNA. Promoters vary, and different cells use different initiation proteins. Yet once a start and its direction are set, RNA grows by adding to its 3′ end. Antiparallel pairing then makes the polymerase read the template 3′ to 5′.
